title: Sign-In Screen and Authentication
brief:
**Project:** Study Group Finder · **Entries close:** [Mon, Oct 5, 6:00 PM ET](https://devdogsuga.org/events/2026-10-05) (start of presentations and judging)

## Summary

Build Dog Pack's sign-in screen and the authentication flow behind it. When you're done, a student can open the app, sign in, stay signed in across restarts, and sign out.

## Background

The Study Group Finder is a Flutter app in [`apps/study-group-finder/`](https://github.com/DevDogsUGA/DevDogsUGA/tree/main/apps/study-group-finder). `lib/main.dart` is still a placeholder. Supabase is already set up there with `supabase_flutter`, so you're building on an existing client.

**How sign-in works (`AUTH_MODE`):** Dog Pack doesn't store its own users. It signs in through the club's shared Supabase project, which sends users to an OAuth provider. The provider depends on `AUTH_MODE`, which `pnpm dev --filter study-group-finder` passes to Flutter as a `--dart-define`. The value comes from `NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_MODE` in the root `.env`.

| `AUTH_MODE` | Where you sign in | Provider ID |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `devdogs` (default, local dev) | The DevDogs platform's own OAuth server ("Sign in with DevDogs") | `custom:devdogsuga` |
| `google` (production) | Google | `google` |

Read it with `String.fromEnvironment('AUTH_MODE')`, as `main.dart` already does. After sign-in, the provider sends the user back to the app at **`dev.dogpack://login-callback`**. That callback is already registered for Android, iOS and Supabase.

Read these first:

- [Study Group Finder docs](https://devdogsuga.org/docs/study-group-finder) and its [first contribution guide](https://devdogsuga.org/docs/study-group-finder/getting-started/first-contribution)
- [DevDogs Flutter sign-in walkthrough](https://devdogsuga.org/docs/workshops/supabase/flutter/02-sign-in)
- [Supabase Flutter `signInWithOAuth` reference](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/dart/auth-signinwithoauth) and [native mobile deep-linking guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/native-mobile-deep-linking)

There is no supplied mockup for this round. Use the existing Material 3 theme and `Color(0xFFBA0C2F)` seed in `main.dart` as the visual starting point, and make the auth states clear, polished and accessible.

## Requirements

- [ ] Build a polished, accessible, Dog Pack-branded sign-in screen.
- [ ] Tapping sign-in starts OAuth with the provider for the current `AUTH_MODE`.
- [ ] After signing in, the user returns to the app through `dev.dogpack://login-callback`.
- [ ] Signed-out users see the sign-in screen. Signed-in users land on the home screen, which has a working sign-out button.
- [ ] A signed-in user is still signed in after restarting the app.
- [ ] Show loading and error states.
- [ ] `flutter analyze` and `flutter test` pass.

## Out of scope

- Other sign-in providers or a provider picker
- Profiles, study groups or anything else past the home screen
- Changes to Supabase or platform configuration

## What we'll test

Judges run every entry on an **Android emulator**.

- Signing in and out in `devdogs` mode
- Cancelling halfway through sign-in
- Denying consent on the provider's screen
- Closing and reopening the app while signed in
- Opening the app with no network connection

## How to submit

1. Work on your team's `team/<your-team>` branch.
2. Open a pull request into `main` with `Closes #<this issue>` in the description.
3. Open it as a **draft PR early**. Only PRs opened before this issue closes are entered.

## Judging

- How well each behavior under "What we'll test" works
- Visual polish, accessibility and clarity across the sign-in, loading, error and home states
- Code quality and readability
- Your PR write-up, including a screen recording of the full flow

The winning entry gets merged into Dog Pack and credited to the team.

title: Time Between Classes I
brief:
**Project:** DogDays · **Entries close:** [Mon, Oct 5, 6:00 PM ET](https://devdogsuga.org/events/2026-10-05) (start of presentations and judging)

## Summary

Let students set both a **minimum** and a **maximum** time between their classes, and make the schedule generator respect both. This round covers class times only. Walking distance between buildings comes in a later round.

## Background

The generator in [`apps/schedule-builder/src/lib/generation/`](https://github.com/DevDogsUGA/DevDogsUGA/tree/main/apps/schedule-builder/src/lib/generation) is a rule engine. Each preference or restriction is a *rule* that plugs into the engine through the hooks in [`rule.ts`](https://github.com/DevDogsUGA/DevDogsUGA/blob/main/apps/schedule-builder/src/lib/generation/rule.ts), and every active rule is listed in `registry.ts`. User inputs reach rules through `GenerationConstraints` in `constraints.ts`.

Read these first:

- [Schedule generation guide](https://devdogsuga.org/docs/schedule-builder/guides/generation), especially "Adding a rule"
- [`rule.ts`](https://github.com/DevDogsUGA/DevDogsUGA/blob/main/apps/schedule-builder/src/lib/generation/rule.ts): read every hook's doc comment carefully before choosing which ones to use
- [`rules/creditHours.ts`](https://github.com/DevDogsUGA/DevDogsUGA/blob/main/apps/schedule-builder/src/lib/generation/rules/creditHours.ts): an existing pair of minimum/maximum rules

## Requirements

- [ ] Add a minimum and a maximum time between classes to `GenerationConstraints`, in minutes. When either one isn't set, it has no effect.
- [ ] Implement the behavior as rules and register them in `registry.ts`. Don't edit `engine.ts`.
- [ ] A student who sets a minimum never sees two classes closer together than that.
- [ ] A student who sets a maximum still gets schedules when nothing fits it, with the closest matches ranked first.
- [ ] Write tests for your rules next to the existing ones in `rules/`.
- [ ] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` pass.

For this competition, the **time between classes** is measured between consecutive classes on the same weekday. It runs from the end of one class to the start of the next, and it doesn't include time before your first class or after your last class of the day.

## Out of scope

- Any UI, saved preferences or server action changes. The inputs get wired into the app in a later issue.
- Walking distance and building locations
- Changes to `engine.ts` or other rules

## What we'll test

- Two classes closer together than the minimum never appear in the same schedule.
- A gap exactly equal to the minimum is allowed.
- A gap that's too long early in the search can be filled by a course added later.
- Sections that meet on the same weekday but in different parts of the term
- A lecture and a lab belonging to the same section
- Days with a single class, and classes before the first or after the last class of the day
- Classes with no set meeting time (online/TBA)
- When nothing satisfies the maximum, schedules are still returned, closest first.
- With neither value set, generation behaves exactly as it does today.

## How to submit

1. Work on your team's `team/<your-team>` branch.
2. Open a pull request into `main` with `Closes #<this issue>` in the description.
3. Open it as a **draft PR early**. Only PRs opened before this issue closes are entered.

## Judging

- Correctness against the behaviors listed under "What we'll test"
- Code quality and readability
- Your own tests
- Your PR write-up: what you built, why, and how a reviewer can check it

The winning entry gets merged into DogDays and credited to the team.
